Re: RBL+ zone - poor performance w 9.2.1
quotation
It's been said the the current focus of BIND 9 is DNSSEC. (See archives.)
I'm sure everyone involved with development is attempting to respond to
all requests in as timely a manner as possible, but there are only so many
things a limited number of people can work on at once. This is not
intended to be patronizing, I'm just restating a point I think we all
agree is valid.

With that said, I've seen this brought up numerous times here and
elsewhere. I've also read numerous whitepapers, articles, etc. citing
"worse" performance in BIND 9. Of course BIND 9 is a complete rewrite and
adds so much functionality that a real comparison by anyone other than the
developers is somewhat absurd (IMCO).

With all of that established, it would seem that the "problem" could be
worked around from an operations standpoint. There are a lot of creative
ways you can cause incoming queries to be redirected to a server that is
not currently reloading the mentioned zone... Why not do that, and at
least minimize the impact on your customers?

One example (typed on the fly, feel free to point out any issues or
modify/enhance as needed),

+---------+ 10.2.3.10
technical
log
tabular
1.2.3.4 and 1.2.3.5 are the external addresses of your nameservers. Fw1
does filtering and NAT. Typically, 1.2.3.4 is staticly NATted to
10.2.3.10 and 1.2.3.5 to 10.2.3.12. However, the unused 10.2.3.11 and
log
return the same answers to DNS queries... So we have two nameservers, but
four addresses serving the same data in the example above.

When it is time for ns1 to reload the problematic zone, we simply rewrite
the static NAT entry on fw1 to point 1.2.3.4 to 10.2.3.13 (ns2-int alias).
Now any queries to ns1 actually get answered by ns2. This is temporary,
of course, and the static NAT entry is rewritten again once the zone
successfully loads on ns1.

It's more work, I'm sure there are caveats, everyone may not want or be
able to do NAT, etc, etc... However, it may be easy enough to think of a
creative way to "fix" the problem from the perspective of your users
(until the BIND folks find the time), that it would be worthwile to
investigate...

package. I've made pretty good progress and have a somewhat functional
gpsd.exe and gpspipe.exe, as tested on Wine and WinXP. The code is
based on the gpsd-2.90 release.

The applicable files are available here:
http://adsllc.fedorapeople.org/gpsd-2.90-mingw/

things before I do much more polishing & fixing.

The basic summary of the changes are:

A. Added win32_compat.* files to compartmentalize as much as possible.
There are still many empty stubs here.
B. Update a bunch of #include stuff to make step A work.
C. Added a serial_win32.c file that is used instead of serial.c as
necessary.
D. Sped up the select() timeout in the main loop on Win32.
E. Added a conditional gps_handle to gps_data_t.
F. Passed the whole gps_data_t* structure in some places instead of just
the fd so gps_handle would be available.
G. The "boolean" token used by the JSON stuff is already defined in
Win32. Renamed to "booleanval".
